html:
From 1964 to 1973 the United States bombed Laos in a secret campaign, first against communist forces in the north and then along the Ho Chi Minh trail. It dropped over two million tons of bombs, making Laos the most heavily bombed country per person in history.

The war was never declared, and the American public learned of it only slowly. Villages on the Plain of Jars were flattened, and people lived for years in caves.

Millions of small cluster bomblets failed to explode. Since the war they have killed or maimed tens of thousands of Laotians, many of them children and farmers, and clearing them goes on. See Laotian Civil War.
